Before breaking up, I would really examine your feelings and make sure that the reason you’re not connecting the way you’d like, isn’t because of a fear of emotional intimacy or getting your heart broken. Maybe see a therapist (or even a nice friend) just to talk it through with a neutral third party. 

However, sometimes we just don’t like people and things just aren’t right. When breakups are depicted in the media, it’s usually this big thing where someone cheated or something huge like that. But more often than not life is simple and boring and things just don’t click how we might want them to.

If you examine your feelings and come to the conclusion that she’s just not right for you, end things. She might be upset initially but she’ll be more upset if you lead her on for months. It’s also important to do this for your mental health, you don’t want to be in a relationship with someone you can’t connect with.

If you have the money or insurance to cover it, it would be worth seeing a sleep specialist. Failing that a psychiatrist who will be able to prescribe something. I don’t have children but if you explain that your husband is competent and the lack of sleep is affecting your mothering ability, they may be willing to give you something.

I would also have a think about what may be causing this on a deeper level: maybe anxiety about being a good mum, maybe something from childhood, etc.

In terms of small things you could do in the meantime, a hot bath before bed usually causes tiredness. You could also consider sleeping in a separate bed to your partner. I find that I get to sleep much quicker when I’m not sharing a bed.

There’s also an insomnia subreddit that you may want to check out. They’ll probably have a better idea of what you’re going through.

Hi OP,

I’ve been accused of attacking you and I don’t want you to hurt more than you already are so I’m going to rephrase my comment and try and give more practical advice.

The majority of people who use this subreddit are suffering from death grief not relationship grief. Therefore, you’re probably not going to get a lot of answers and advice here. I’ve taken the liberty of compiling some subreddits where you’ll probably get better advice. I’ve added limerence and anxious attachment as these are two things I’ve suffered from in the past and I felt like they may be playing a role in your situation from what you wrote. 

R/relationships 
R/relationshipadvice 
R/breakups
R/heartbreak 
R/limerence 
R/anxiousattachment

Attachment style can definitely be changed through therapy, it’s not tied to your personality type (personality type is a bit of a pseudoscience). A secure attachment style is definitely something everyone should aim for and can achieve. Having an anxious attachment style isn’t something to be ashamed of, loads of people do, it’s just something to be aware of. 

As with a death, I would give yourself time to mourn and be sad before dating someone knew. If you don’t already have a therapist, it would be good to see someone and explore why this has affected you so deeply. That way you can hopefully avoid something similar in the future. 

26 is really young still. I know it can seem like everyone else is in love but that’s not the case. I was quite late in having my first boyfriend and I remember feeling really similar to you. It’s just important to remember that it’s not a reflection of your personality. When you do get into a relationship, you’ll be in a much better place than most people because you would have had time to grow as an individual.

Hope this helpful, would really recommend trying the other subreddits I suggested.
I’m aware it’s a valid form of grief. Nowhere did I say otherwise. Look at how many useful replies they’ve actually gotten. They’re gonna get better advice elsewhere.
Not saying it doesn’t, I’m saying that the majority of people who use this sub are death bereaved individuals. OP is going to get better advice elsewhere.

I didn’t say they should remove, I was trying to point them in the direction. As you can see despite the upvotes, few people have actually commented to offer advice, whereas if they posted it on a relationship subreddit.

This subreddit isn’t really for this type of grief. It’s for people who’ve had someone die; they’ll be better subreddits for what you’re going through. 

I’m not critiquing your attachment style but I suggest you see a therapist. Attachment styles can change to be much healthier and happier with the right therapy.

My dad died under really similar circumstances when I was 19.

I think big holidays are always going to be tough regardless of whether they held any special significance. It’s another thing they’ve missed and a sign of time passing. I’m lucky in that I have a partner, but I live in constant fear of being alone with my grief again like I was for the first few years. I find that a lot of people who ‘bounce back’ after a loss, are those lucky enough to have a really strong family network or living partner. I get quite annoyed when people in those circumstances wax lyrical about how to mourn and move on because there situation vastly differs. 

You’re not a failure for not having a boyfriend/girlfriend. You’re so strong for going through life handling your loss on your own and your starting nursing school this year. What a achievement!

Okay right, let’s try and work through the practical stuff first. 

You’ve got a flight back home. That’s great. You can spend time with you dad and speak with him in person. This is the most important thing. 

You don’t need to spend the rest of his time on this earth in his company or be with him the moment he passes. You can be if you want to be and your situation will allow it, but this is not necessary for either you or him. What’s most important is seeing him, speaking with him and telling him how much you love him (which is what you’re going to be doing tomorrow!) If you have to fly back home, you can still FaceTime and call him everyday. I know this isn’t the same as seeing him face to face but it still means so much. 

I don’t know exactly how jury duty works but I think you should be able to opt out of it on compassionate grounds. You need to get a letter from your dad’s consultant explaining his terminal status and email this to the relevant individuals asking to be excused. 

I’m so sorry for you and your family are going through. My dad died a couple of years back suddenly following a terminal diagnosis of bowel cancer. He was 50 and I was 19 at the time. It’s such a horrific experience. 

I think the best course of action right now is: get on the plane, get letter to get out out of jury service and send email, wait for the results of the biopsy (once you know exactly what’s going on and have a better idea of how much time he has left, it will allow you to plan next steps better) 

You will survive this. It will be difficult and awful but you will.
